svg.title: How a checkride run works once a repo has targets
svg.desc: A repo's toolchain markers become targets, each a language pack at a root, plus repo-wide checks. Every check then resolves an adapter, is selected, scheduled, launched through its pack's pin chain and captured, and the baseline decides the verdict. The run writes a summary and raw output per target, which the findings API, triage, the gate and a PR-review agent read.
svg.text: How a run works once a repo has targets
Same engine as 0.13: spawn each tool, keep its raw output, gate on its exit code.
What's new is around it: targets, language packs, pin chains, and runs shaped from outside the repo.
shapes a run from outside the repo
× no target claims tools/gen/, so unclaimed fails
Targets come from targets in config, checkride target add, or --discover at run time (in memory, nothing written).
Every pack shares the slot names and brings its own tools: types runs tsc, go build, cargo check, mypy or terraform validate.
Target checks are named api:lint and write under <out>/api/; repo-wide checks keep bare names.
No targets and no --discover: implicit mode, which is 0.13 exactly.
One unnamed target at the root, its pack picked by the first marker found there: ts, go, rust, python or terraform.
The first source that names an adapter wins; the check records it as origin.
Tokens: lint (every target), api (one target), api:lint (one check).
--changed diffs from the merge base of --base; untouched targets skip,
and Go narrows go build and go test to the affected modules.
--static-only keeps only checks that read the repo as data, with no install.
Waves by order, as in 0.13. Checks that share a lock key never overlap,
such as cargo:<root>; waiting for a lock doesn't count toward the timeout.
native = package.json · go.mod tool · rust-toolchain · uv.lock · .terraform-version
The first declaring source wins, with no fall-through to another copy.
Runs from the target root with downloads off (GOPROXY=off, UV_OFFLINE, …).
A declared outputFile keeps JSON as .json and JSON lines as .jsonl;
everything else stays byte for byte in .stdout.txt and .stderr.txt.
failOnOutput fails a tool that exits 0 but still prints findings, and a
custom check's skipExitCode records a skip instead of a red or a false green.
The baseline subtracts grandfathered findings, keyed on gating findings only
and repo-relative paths. Exit 0 green, 1 red, 2 when the harness itself broke.
Only the repo's own full run ratchets the baseline; outside runs write nothing.
WHAT A RUN WRITES, AND WHO READS IT
run, git, targets; per check origin, pin_source, argv
markers no target claims, with a suggested target
repo-wide raw output, one file per slot
one folder per target: lint.json, test.json, …
ratcheted only by the repo's own full run
file, line, rule, severity, and whether it gates.
Runs the repo's own check into <repo>/.check/,
A --static-only pass before its sandbox, then a
full pass inside it, each with its own --out.
† schema arrives in Phase 12. It and the standalone binary (Phase 13) stay last; whether to build them is decided after Phase 11.
